result.text:
# Vacuum-salt plant, vapour recompression evaporator: data sheet

REAL DESIGN DATA from US Patent 5,366,514 (Texas Brine Corp., 1994), FIG. 1 and Table I: a 2,500 short-ton-per-day
plant making 99.99 % NaCl from solution-mined brine. The drawing is the patent's FIG. 1; numbers in brackets are the
patent's reference numerals. Equipment ratings marked ILLUSTRATIVE are not in the patent.

## Operating point (patent Table I, converted to SI)
| Stream / item | Value |
|---|---|
| Feed brine to the brine cooled condenser (3) (stream 2), "saturated in salt" (about 26 wt % NaCl) | 362.9 t/h at 24 °C |
| Brine leaving the brine cooled condenser | 60 °C |
| Elutriating brine to the evaporator legs (streams 7, 8) | 98.0 t/h at 60 °C |
| Brine through the brine preheater BP (10) to the VRC evaporator (12) (streams 9/11) | 264.9 t/h, 60 → 125.6 °C |
| VRC evaporator (12) | 1.70 bar(a) (10 psig), brine boiling at 125.6 °C |
| VRC evaporator overhead to the VRC compressor (26) (stream 25) | 226.8 t/h steam, saturation 115.2 °C at 1.70 bar(a) |
| VRC compressor (26) discharge | 3.08 bar(a) (30 psig), pressure ratio 1.8 |
| Desuperheated steam to the circulating heater CH1 (stream 36), incl. 15.9 t/h turbine exhaust (stream 33) | 251.7 t/h at 135 °C, 3.08 bar(a) |
| CH1 condensate (stream 21) | 251.7 t/h at 134.4 °C, cooled in BP (10) to about 82 °C |
| Excess VRC evaporator vapour to the purge heater CH2 (stream 31) | 20.9 t/h |
| Purge liquor, VRC evaporator → purge evaporator (5) (stream 14) | 47.6 t/h at 125.6 °C |
| Purge evaporator (5) | about 1.01 bar(a), 108.9 °C |
| Purge to the disposal well facility (18) (stream 16) | 6.8 t/h at 108.9 °C |
| Purge-evaporator overheads to the brine cooled condenser (stream 4) | 25.4 t/h at 100.6 °C after desuperheating |
| Salt produced (dry) (17) | 94.9 t/h (2,511 short t/d) |

The patent describes the FIG. 1 feed as "saturated in salt". It explicitly allows lower-concentration feed; solution-mined
brine can arrive below saturation. Use `feed_x_NaCl` to examine that case rather than treating 26 wt % as universal.

## What the patent says about the equipment
- The VRC compressor (26) is a single-wheel centrifugal compressor, 1.8:1, driven by the combustion gas turbine (37). "The VRC
  compressor can only pass a fixed amount of steam": the vapour above its suction capacity (about 90 % of the boil-up passes
  it) is the excess sent to the purge evaporator heater CH2 (patent col. 7-8).
- Desuperheating condensate is sprayed into the compressor discharge because superheated steam transfers heat poorly in the
  large circulating heaters (col. 7). The desuperheater is not drawn in FIG. 1.

## Equipment ratings
- VRC compressor (26) suction capacity: 226.8 t/h (the patent's fixed compressor throughput). Shaft power: not stated in the patent.
- Circulating heater CH1: 8,800 m², U 2,000 W/m²K in service (ILLUSTRATIVE; 2,500 W/m²K clean).
- Forced-circulation pump of the VRC evaporator (not drawn in FIG. 1): 15,000 m³/h rated (ILLUSTRATIVE).
- Purge heater CH2: 1,500 m², U 1,500 W/m²K (ILLUSTRATIVE).

## Process requirements and design rules
- Brine temperature rise through CH1 at most 3 K: a larger rise flashes in the tubes and scales them with salt.
- Condensate leaves CH1 saturated at the shell pressure.
- The brine boils above the steam saturation temperature by its boiling point elevation (use the brine_bpe tool).

## Modelling scope (from the plant's process engineer)
- The capacity question is decided by the VRC loop: VRC evaporator (12) boil-up, VRC compressor (26), the discharge
  desuperheating and the circulating heater CH1, plus the purge evaporator (5) with CH2 that takes the excess vapour.
  Model that loop in detail.
- The feed preheat train (brine cooled condenser, BP) is not in question: take the brine entering the VRC evaporator from
  Table I (264.9 t/h at 125.6 °C, plus 98.0 t/h elutriating brine at 60 °C, both scaling with throughput) instead of
  closing the condensate-to-brine heat-recovery loops.
- Turbine exhaust steam joining the compressor discharge (stream 33): 15.9 t/h at 3.08 bar(a), fixed (the gas turbine does
  not grow with salt production).

## Request
Sales wants the plant to make **3,000 short tons per day instead of 2,500 (+20 %)**.

submit.headline: No — plant cannot reach higher salt rate
submit.summary: As built, the simulator at +20% throughput (run target-1.2 / sweep of as-built-base) puts the vapour recompressor VRC-1 at 102.5% of its 226.8 t/h suction rating and the main evaporator VRE-1 heat supply at 101.7%, so 3,000 short tons/day is not reachable without changes; cleaning the main heater alone leaves both at 102.5%/101.7%. Files produced: sweep chart 20261101-012154-original-model-ch1-u-at-1-2x-throughput- (sweep.svg, sweep.json).

cards.title: Can it make 3,000 short tons per day?
cards.result: No as built — compressor and main heater over limits

inputs.name: Present salt rate
inputs.source: Data sheet Table I, salt produced row

inputs.name: VRC-1 suction capacity
inputs.source: P&ID tag VRC-1; data sheet Equipment ratings, VRC compressor suction capacity

assumptions: Feeds S11 264.9 t/h at 125.6 C and S7 98.0 t/h at 60 C scale with throughput, per data sheet Modelling scope (documented).
Turbine exhaust feed S33 stays fixed at 15.9 t/h, per data sheet Modelling scope (documented).
Feed brine is 26 wt% NaCl saturated, per data sheet Table I (documented for this operating point, not universal).

cards.title: What limits it first?
cards.result: Main heater heat supply first, compressor tightest at +20%

inputs.name: First limit on a throughput ramp
inputs.value: VRE-1 boil-up duty vs heat from heating steam, 100% at 0.921x

inputs.source: process_capacity on as-built-base, checks at base

inputs.name: VRC-1 at base rate
inputs.source: process_capacity on as-built-base, checks at base

inputs.name: PE-1 at base rate
inputs.source: process_capacity on as-built-base, checks at base

inputs.name: CH1 installed area / in-service U
inputs.source: P&ID tag VRE-1 (includes CH1); data sheet Equipment ratings CH1 — marked ILLUSTRATIVE

assumptions: Conclusion is provisional: the plant is modelled essentially at its heat-balance limit at base rate (100.6%), within the model's 2% closure tolerance, so the exact ramp point is uncertain — the +20% verdict is not, both key checks exceed 100% there.

cards.title: Cheapest fix tested: clean the main heater
cards.result: Helps area only — still 102.5% compressor, 101.7% heat

inputs.name: CH1 clean U
inputs.source: Data sheet Equipment ratings CH1 (ILLUSTRATIVE, not in patent)

assumptions: Cleaning is the cheapest physical step and is worth doing for area margin, but the simulator shows it does not create steam: the limits are steam flow (compressor) and steam heat supply, not area.

cards.title: Most economical route to +20%
cards.result: Divert excess vapour to purge unit plus added steam — provisional

inputs.name: Design intent for excess vapour
inputs.value: Vapour above compressor capacity goes to purge heater CH2 / PE-1
inputs.source: Data sheet, patent description of VRC compressor (col. 7-8) and stream 31 row (20.9 t/h)

inputs.name: Split needed at +20% to hold compressor at rating
inputs.value: About 89.3% to compressor / 10.7% excess, vs 91.57% / 8.43% now
inputs.source: Derived from logged sweep utilisation 102.5% at scale 1.2 on as-built-base

inputs.name: Extra steam source
inputs.value: Not documented — no HRSG/duct-firing capacity on P&ID or data sheet
inputs.source: P&ID tags CGT-1/HRSG-1/ST-1 (no capacity data); data sheet fixes stream 33 at 15.9 t/h

assumptions: Provisional: diverting vapour alone starves CH1 of returning steam, so it only works paired with supplementary steam into the discharge header; that steam source is not in the model or documents and must be confirmed before this route can be claimed to reach 3,000 short t/d.
If no supplementary steam is available, the fallback is new compression capacity in parallel with VRC-1 — highest cost, not proposed in detail because no vendor rating exists in the documents.

highlights.text: Suction 102.5% of 226.8 t/h rating at +20% (sweep of as-built-base, scale 1.2) — tightest check at target.
Heat supply 101.7% at +20% and first limit on a ramp (100% at 0.921x, process_capacity); area 96.7% at in-service U 2,000. Includes CH1.
Heat supply 98.0% at +20% — little margin if more excess vapour is diverted to CH2. Includes CH2.
No steam-generation or duct-firing capacity documented; supplementary steam route cannot be verified from P&ID/data sheet.
Drives VRC-1; shaft power not stated in patent/data sheet, so extra compression power cannot be checked.

proposals.title: Send more vapour around the compressor to the purge evaporator
proposals.why: Operating-only change: lifting the excess-vapour share from 8.43% to about 10.7% brings VRC-1 suction back to its documented 226.8 t/h rating at +20%. It must be paired with supplementary steam (see field checks) or CH1 loses returning heat; the workspace re-solve will show this.

proposals.title: Clean the main circulating heater CH1 back to clean performance
proposals.why: Cheapest physical step: restores area margin at +20% (96.7% utilised at fouled U). The sweep shows it does not by itself fix the 101.7% heat-supply or 102.5% compressor limits, so it is an enabling step, not the whole fix.

changes.physical_change: Clean CH1 (in VRE-1) tubes to restore documented clean heat-transfer performance
changes.rating_source: Data sheet Equipment ratings: CH1 clean U 2,500 W/m2K — marked ILLUSTRATIVE, vendor/cleaning record to confirm

field_checks.item: Supplementary steam availability for the discharge header (HRSG-1 duct firing or boiler capacity, fuel and steam-turbine/generator knock-on)
field_checks.where: HRSG-1 / ST-1 / CGT-1 vendor data and plant steam balance; confirm how many t/h above the fixed 15.9 t/h stream 33 can be supplied at 3.08 bar(a)
field_checks.changes: Decides the recommended route: if roughly the CH1 heat shortfall at +20% cannot be supplied as extra steam, the reroute proposal fails and parallel compression capacity (>$1M) is the only route to 3,000 short t/d.

field_checks.item: CH1 clean heat-transfer coefficient and whether current U is really 2,000 W/m2K
field_checks.where: CH1 vendor datasheet and recent operating temperatures/flows around VRE-1 heating (streams S36/S21_COND); both values are marked ILLUSTRATIVE in the data sheet
field_checks.changes: If clean U is below 2,500, VRE-1 area (96.7% at +20% fouled) becomes the binding limit and added area, not just cleaning, is needed.

field_checks.item: Feed brine salt concentration (model assumes saturated 26 wt%)
field_checks.where: Sample/lab analysis of feed brine at BPF-1 inlet (stream 2) over a week
field_checks.changes: The patent allows below-saturation feed; lower concentration means more water to evaporate per ton of salt, making every limit above worse and moving the required steam/compression up.

field_checks.item: Forced-circulation rate and brine temperature rise through CH1 (design rule: at most 3 K)
field_checks.where: Circulation pump flow (rated 15,000 m3/h, ILLUSTRATIVE) and CH1 brine in/out temperatures at VRE-1
field_checks.changes: Not a modelled check; if the 3 K rule is already approached, raising circulation or heat flux for +20% risks salt scaling in the tubes regardless of the steam-side fix.
